title: Big number puzzles
goal: I can read, compare and round numbers up to 10 million. I can test both sides of a target and check every clue.

learn.intro: Read a big number in groups of three from the right. To find the number closest to a target, test the best number just below it and just above it.

example.problem: Use the cards to make a 7-digit number as close as you can to 3 000 000. Use every card once. A number cannot start with 0.
steps: Just below the target: start with 2. Then put the cards in order from greatest to smallest: 2 985 310.
Just above the target: start with 3. Then put the rest in order from smallest to greatest: 3 012 589.
Compare the gaps. 12 589 is smaller than 14 690, so the number above is closer.

howto.title: Closest number
steps: Write the best number just below the target.
Write the best number just above the target.
Find the gap for each. The smaller gap wins.

facts.title: Place-value chart
lines: M is millions. TTh is ten-thousands.

try.text: Use the cards to make a 7-digit number as close as you can to 8 000 000. Use every card once. Write your number. {l}
try.explanation: Just below 8 000 000: start with 7, then the greatest order: 7 964 310 (35 690 away). Just above: start with 9, then the smallest order: 9 013 467 (1 013 467 away). 7 964 310 is closer.

items.text: Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the number: 6 million, 205 thousand and 30. {l}

items.explanation: (a) 6 million, 205 thousand, 30: the hundreds place is empty, so 6 205 030. (b) The 7 is in the ten thousands place: 70 000. (c) 8 604 000 ÷ 1000 = 8604.
940 621 has 6 digits, so it is smallest. Then compare 4 096 213, 4 096 231 and 4 906 213 digit by digit.

items.text: Round 7 849 520 to the nearest:
items.explanation: Look at the digit after the place. (a) 849 520: the hundreds digit is 5, so 7 850 000. (b) 49 520 is under 50 000, so 7 800 000. (c) 849 520 is over 500 000, so 8 000 000.

items.text: Look at the cards. Use all 7 cards once in each answer. A number cannot start with 0.
items.explanation: (a) A multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5. Ending in 0: 9 875 410. Ending in 5 gives only 9 874 105. (b) Start with 1, then 0, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9: 1 045 789.

items.text: Ben has the number below. He adds 2 hundred-thousands. Then he takes away 5 ten-thousands. What is Ben's new number?
Estimate each answer by rounding. Circle one choice for each.
items.explanation: (a) 4000 × 50 = 200 000, but 20 722 is far too small. (b) 4 million + 3 million is about 7 million: close. (c) 8000 × 300 = 2 400 000: close. (d) 6000 ÷ 15 = 400, so 4050 is 10 times too big.

items.text: Put ONE pair of brackets in each line to make it true. Write the new line.
A factory makes 1 250 000 bolts. It packs 500 bolts in each box. Each carton holds 24 boxes. How many full cartons can it fill? {b} cartons
items.explanation: 1 250 000 ÷ 500 = 2500 boxes. Then 2500 ÷ 24 = 104 remainder 4, since 24 × 104 = 2496. Only full cartons count, so 104.

items.text: A number rounded to the nearest hundred is 8 700. Fill in the blanks.
items.explanation: The halfway marks are 8650 and 8750. 8650 rounds up to 8700, so it counts. 8750 rounds up to 8800, so the greatest is 8749.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The greatest 6-digit number is 1 less than the smallest 7-digit number.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which town has the most people? {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many more people live in the town with the most people than in the town with the fewest? {l}

items.explanation: (a) Compare the hundred thousands: Dune has 4. (b) Cedar is smallest: 1 420 050 - 1 024 500 = 395 550.

items.text: Solve the riddle in the box. Check every clue when you finish.

lines: I round to 470 000 when rounded to
My hundreds digit is twice my tens digit.

items.explanation: Clue 2: from 465 000 to 474 999. Clue 3 gives 472. Clue 5: ones 0. Clue 4: tens 3 and hundreds 6 (the pairs 1 and 2, or 4 and 8, repeat a digit). So 472 630.

items.text: A stadium has 48 000 seats. On Monday 3 100 people came. On Tuesday twice as many came. On Wednesday 1 250 fewer people came than on Tuesday. How many people came in all? {l} people
items.explanation: Monday 3100, Tuesday 6200, Wednesday 4950. Total 14 250. The 48 000 is not needed.

items.text:
Circle every number that rounds to 5 000 000 when rounded to the nearest million.
{circ:4 499 999|4 500 000|5 499 999|5 500 000}
items.explanation: Numbers from 4 500 000 to 5 499 999 round to 5 000 000.

items.text: Solve the riddle in the box. Test the clues one at a time.

lines: I round to 6 400 000 when rounded to
My ten-thousands digit is 1 less than
My hundreds digit is 2 more than

items.hint: Clues 2 and 3 fix the first 3 digits. Then use Clue 6.
items.explanation: Clue 2: 6 350 000 to 6 449 999. Clue 3 leaves 6 4 3. The tens digit is 0. The other 3 digits add to 33 - 6 - 4 - 3 - 0 = 20. Thousands t and hundreds t + 2: t = 5 gives 5, 7 and ones 8. So 6 435 708.

items.text: Every number from 195 000 to 204 999 rounds to 200 000 when rounded to the nearest ten-thousand.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many of these numbers have a digit sum of 4? {b}

items.hint: Numbers from 195 000 to 199 999 have a digit sum over 4.
items.explanation: Below 200 000 the digits 1 + 9 are already 10. So the number is 20 _ _ _ _ with the other digits adding to 2: 4 ways with one 2 and 6 ways with two 1s. Total 10.

items.text: Use each card once to make a 3-digit number and a 2-digit number. Multiply the 2 numbers. Make the product as great as you can.
items.hint: The greatest digits go first. Try both ways.
items.explanation: Put the greatest digits first: 9 and 7. 752 × 93 = 69 936 beats 953 × 72 = 68 616 and 732 × 95 = 69 540.

items.text: The first digit is never 0. How many 7-digit numbers have 7 different digits? {l}
items.hint: Count the choices for the first digit, then the second.
items.explanation: First digit: 9 choices (1 to 9). Second: 9 choices (0 is allowed). Then 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. 9 × 9 × 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 × 4 = 544 320.

items.text: Ali writes down every whole number from 1 to 999. He adds up all the digits he wrote. What is the total? {l}
items.hint: Write 7 as 007. Each digit 0 to 9 appears equally often.
items.explanation: Write 7 as 007. The numbers 000 to 999 are 1000 numbers. In each of the 3 places every digit 0 to 9 appears 100 times, adding 4500. 3 × 4500 = 13 500.

items.text: Use each of 3, 4, 7 and 9 once. You may use + - × ÷ and brackets. What is the number closest to 100 that you can make? {b}
items.hint: 9 × 11 is 99, but 11 is hard to make. Try 3 × 4 × 9.
items.explanation: 3 × 4 × 9 - 7 = 101, which is 1 away. 99 and 100 cannot be made, and 102 is 2 away. So 101.

items.text: A printing press prints 2 400 sheets in 1 hour. It runs for 8 hours each day. A shop needs 1 000 000 sheets. How many days does the press need? {b} days
items.hint: Sheets in one day first. Then divide. Is the answer a whole number?
items.explanation: 2400 × 8 = 19 200 sheets a day. 52 days give 998 400, not enough, so 53 days.

items.text: Look at the number 5 280 436.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Rounded to the nearest 100 000, it is {l}

items.explanation: (a) The 2 is in the hundred thousands place: 200 000. (b) 5 280 436: the ten thousands digit is 8, so round up to 5 300 000.

items.text: Build the 7-digit number nearest to 4 000 000. Use each card once.
items.explanation: Just below: 3 976 520 (23 480 away). Just above: 5 023 679 (1 023 679 away). The first is closer.

items.text: Put ONE pair of brackets in 8 + 12 ÷ 4 × 2 = 10 to make it true. Write the new line. {ll}
items.explanation: (8 + 12) ÷ 4 × 2 = 20 ÷ 4 × 2 = 5 × 2 = 10. Without brackets the line gives 8 + 3 × 2 = 14.

items.text: 18 buses each carry 1 250 passengers in a week. How many passengers is that in 12 weeks? {l}
